name: NFL Fantasy Agent

track.name: The Agent That Can Explain Why

users: Fantasy football managers making waiver and lineup decisions

team.name: Justin Chen
contributions: H-MEM conflict detection, sleep cycle and dreaming services

agents.name: Planner
agents.role: Classifies the question type and extracts the player names (one model call; keyword-rule fallback).

agents.name: Analyst
agents.role: Looks the player(s) up and corrects a wrong premise from the rosters table. Runs the planned factor queries through Zetaris, then one factor agent per factor in parallel (rule fallback) and the verdict.
agents.sub_agents: factor_agent:<factor>, one per factor, in parallel

agents.name: Critic
agents.role: Code checks: verdict support, numbers, artifacts, question fit, timing, league memory, compare, no-data, position label, factor direction (by metric polarity), matchup label and bye. Then an optional model review (it can block only in round 1). Blocking issues send the verdict back for revision; if the revision still breaks a hard rule, the round-3 verdict is rule-based and labelled.

features.premise_correction: A wrong team in the question is corrected from the rosters table before the agents answer.
features.league_memory: With a user_id: league size, scoring and roster are stored and retrieved with the H-MEM engine.
features.provenance: Each claim carries its SQL and rows; each reply says which steps a model or the code rules produced.
features.factor_directions: Which player each factor favours is computed in code from each metric's polarity (app/agents/directions.py); a model summary that contradicts it is replaced by the code summary, labelled.
features.matchup_labels: Each opponent's rank in points allowed (1 = allows the most) is labelled in code: 1-10 of 32 favorable, 11-22 neutral, 23-32 tough. The label is in the factor and verdict facts, and wording that contradicts it is blocked.
features.bye_check: With no week named, the target week is the latest stats week + 1; a player on bye gets "Sit <player>" as a hard rule, and the Critic blocks a start.
features.no_data_and_position_checks: The Critic blocks a pick of a player with no data and a player given another position's label (e.g. a TE called WR1).
features.hard_rule_fallback: Hard rules (out player, rostered player, usage pick, compare leader, named player, position label, no data, bye, matchup direction): if the round-2 revision still breaks one, the round-3 verdict is rule-based and labelled instead of looping.
features.disclaimer: Informational only, based on nflverse data; not betting advice.

nightshift.role: Only model provider: every model call goes through its OpenAI-compatible API.
calls: league-memory mining (only when code cannot parse the cues)

engines_used.version: all seven spec services: MemoryStoreService, MemoryRetrievalService, TrustLedgerService, model extraction of MemoryMiningService, ConflictDetectionService, SleepCycleService, DreamingService
engines_used.feature: League memory (app/agents/memory.py), turned on by user_id in POST /run. Scoring and team count are stored, and so are rostered and dropped players. Retrieved records set the scoring of the factor queries, stop rule-based pickups of rostered players and feed critic check (f).
engines_used.where_in_pipeline: app/pipeline.py: memory.remember (store, then retrieve) runs before the Planner
engines_used.conformance: 13/13 checks of the official runner pass (2026-10-25, commit b2d8c7a); 10/13 before the sleep, conflict and dreaming services were added

zetaris.role: All live data. Every fact in an answer comes from a SQL query through run_sql, one statement per call.
zetaris.storage: Parquet on S3, registered as Zetaris Lightning filestore tables
zetaris.sample_mode: SAMPLE_MODE=true runs the same SQL on DuckDB against data/sample/

models.traced_as: model field of model_call trace lines (meterless.routed_model)
models.receipts: Nightshift Console Proof page, one receipt per request (docs/images/nightshift-receipts.png)

cursor: Cursor: not used. The organizers made Cursor optional on 22 October 2026, and #help-desk confirmed it isn't required on 25 October; the project was built in Claude Code.

data_sources.name: nflverse
data_sources.coverage: Season 2026, weeks 1-6 of stats; rosters and depth charts as of week 7; schedules to week 18

data_sources.name: FTN charting data
data_sources.note: Credited as the project requires; the current build does not load the FTN charting table.

entry_points.ui: app/ui/ served by run.py on port 8080

examples: examples/ (live runs; examples/critic-demo-* starts from a saved Analyst answer)
third_party_licences: LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt (Zetaris getting-started adapter code; Meterless H-MEM spec)
